places.desc: a maze of narrow lanes behind the station: racks of secondhand clothes on the pavement, record stores, curry counters, tiny bars, music leaking up from basement stairs
places.staff: shopkeepers hauling clothes racks, buskers with an open guitar case, university students in thrifted coats, bar touts handing out flyers

places.name: Second Bloom
places.desc: a vintage clothing shop up a short stair: racks sorted by decade, a fitting curtain, a record player behind the till, a window dressed for the season
places.staff: the owner, fifties, dry, on a stool by the till; a part-timer steaming coats; shoppers at the mirror

places.name: Basement Moon
places.desc: a basement stage down a steep stair: black walls papered with stickers and flyers, room for a hundred, a bar by the door, a sound desk on a platform at the back
places.staff: a bartender handing out drink tickets, a sound engineer at the desk, bands hauling amps through the crowd

places.name: Theater Komorebi
places.desc: a tiny fringe theater up an outside stair above a bar: sixty folding seats, a stage the size of a living room, a skylight that drops a patch of sun on the boards
places.staff: a stage manager with a clipboard, actors tearing tickets in costume, the bar owner pouring downstairs

places.name: Curry Hanabi
places.desc: a narrow soup-curry shop with eight counter seats and three tables: a pot of spiced soup always simmering, roasted vegetables on the pass, the smell reaching the end of the lane
places.staff: a cook behind the pass, a server calling spice levels, a lunch line down the stairs

places.name: Kissa Shirakaba
places.desc: an old coffee house unchanged since the 1970s: dark wood, brown vinyl booths, a siphon bar, a glass case of plastic food, yellowed lace curtains and a painted birch on the sign
places.staff: the master at the siphons, a waitress with a tray, old regulars with newspapers, a loud wall clock

places.name: Matsu-no-yu
places.desc: an old bathhouse behind a pine-painted curtain: a temple-style roof, wooden-tagged shoe lockers, a raised attendant's seat at the door, and a mural of Mt. Fuji over each bath
places.staff: the attendant on the raised seat, the owner mopping tiles, grandmothers gossiping, workers straight from a job site

places.name: Kōenji's covered arcade
places.desc: a covered shopping arcade off the station: secondhand clothes, record shops, izakaya, a fishmonger, rolling shutters, bicycles under the lamps, a different smell every ten steps
places.staff: shopkeepers calling out, aunties with shopping carts, a man tuning a guitar by the bicycles, bar touts

places.name: Moonlight Mart Kōenji
places.desc: a 24-hour convenience store by the station: bright white light, a hot case by the register, rice-ball shelves, an ATM in the corner and a door chime that never stops
places.staff: a clerk greeting each customer, a stocker filling the lunch shelf, late-night regulars, a salaryman buying a sports drink

places.name: Studio Tsubame
places.desc: a small anime studio in a converted two-story house: shoes off at the entrance, desks crammed under hanging lamps, stacks of paper, a rice cooker in the kitchen that never switches off
places.staff: animators bent over light boxes, a production assistant chasing late pages, someone asleep under a desk

places.name: Electric Town
places.desc: the main street of Akihabara under towering signs: parts stalls beneath the tracks, capsule-toy walls, used-figure shops, cosplayers photographing each other; on Sunday afternoons the cars vanish
places.staff: stall owners calling prices, maids with menu boards, solo travelers, fans with heavy bags, cosplayers in side streets

places.name: Café Mille-Feuille
places.desc: a maid café up a narrow staircase: pink and cream walls, a stage the size of a table, a menu of omurice with ketchup pictures, and staff who greet everyone with "welcome home"
places.staff: maids in uniform playing characters, a calm cook in the kitchen, regulars with notebooks, first-timers who don't know where to look

places.name: Pixel Castle
places.desc: a seven-floor game center: prize machines at the door, rhythm cabinets upstairs, a floor of photo booths, a medal-game hall on top, and a thump of music that never stops
places.staff: staff in headsets nudging prizes, salarymen after work, couples at the photo booths, players waiting in silence for the rhythm cabinets

places.name: Stage Starlight
places.desc: a small idol theater in a basement: a stage a step above the floor, a ceiling of fairy lights, a merch table by the door, a hundred seats and a cheki corner
places.staff: the theater's manager at the door, a sound engineer behind the desk, trainers in the rehearsal room, front-row regulars, new fans in rows

places.name: Mochi Byte Games
places.desc: an indie studio on the second floor of a narrow building: standing desks, a wall of sticky notes, a rice-cake mascot on every monitor, and a smell of instant noodles and coffee
places.staff: developers in headphones, an artist drawing on a tablet, a producer on the phone, playtesters waiting by the demo kiosk

places.name: Comic Cocoon
places.desc: a manga and internet café over several floors: shelves to the ceiling, private booths with reclining seats and curtains, a drink bar, a shower room, and a hush broken by page-turns
places.staff: a clerk at the desk with a ticket machine, people asleep in booths, a salaryman with a bag on his lap, gamers with headphones

places.name: Kanda Myōjin
places.desc: the old shrine of merchants on a hill of red lacquer and green copper roofs: a great gate, an ema wall covered in anime drawings, and engineers buying charms for their computers
places.staff: priests and miko at the charm office, fans photographing the ema, office workers praying for a deal, neighbors sweeping leaves

places.name: Jinbōchō book town
places.desc: street after street of used bookshops with carts out front, ink and old paper in the air, a curry house with a line, and coffee shops tucked between the shelves
places.staff: elderly shop owners behind piles of books, readers standing in aisles, a queue outside a curry house, solo travelers with heavy bags

places.name: Seiran Prep School, Ochanomizu
places.desc: a prep school in a glass-fronted tower in Ochanomizu: lecture halls, a hushed self-study room, vending machines on every landing and a bulletin board of exam results
places.staff: teachers with handouts, candidates with highlighters and instant noodles, a receptionist handling enrollments, a tired monitor in the study room

places.name: Hijiri University
places.desc: a university campus by the Ochanomizu bridges: brick lecture halls, a language center in an old annex, a library that never has a free seat, a row of club rooms
places.staff: lecturers with laptops, third-years in club jackets, exchange students in the stairwell, a library desk, vending machines on every floor

places.name: Sensō-ji & Nakamise
places.desc: Tokyo's oldest temple behind the red Thunder Gate: incense smoke over the main hall, a pagoda beyond, and Nakamise, the lane of snack and souvenir stalls where rickshaws wait
places.staff: stall keepers calling out sweets, a monk sweeping, a company outing behind a flag, pullers in happi coats

places.name: Sumida riverside
places.desc: a river walk lined with cherry trees, water buses sliding past, and the Skytree standing tall across the water; benches, joggers and a breeze that smells of the river
places.staff: joggers, an old man feeding pigeons, couples on the benches, a water-bus conductor, street sketchers

places.name: Izakaya Daruma
places.desc: an open-front stew-and-beer shop with no sign on a lantern-lit lane near Sensō-ji: crates for stools, a pot of stew that never leaves the flame, a daruma doll with one eye painted watching the till
places.staff: the stout owner shouts orders; a cook stirs the pot; old men and salarymen share tables spilling onto the lane

places.name: Ueno Park
places.desc: a huge park of museums, the lotus pond and the zoo gate, with broad avenues of cherry trees and street performers on the plaza
places.staff: joggers, sketchers with easels, a juggler on the plaza, boat attendants, couples and friends at the zoo gate

places.name: Ueno Hall of Art
places.desc: a quiet art museum in the park: stone steps and tall windows, a hall of Japanese paintings and prints, a new special exhibition each season, and a café on the ground floor
places.staff: guards in soft shoes, a ticket clerk, guides in navy blazers, couples on a slow weekday and university art students sketching

places.name: Ameyoko
places.desc: a loud market street along and under the railway tracks: fishmongers shouting prices, dried-goods stalls, spice shops, sneakers and bargain bins, trains rattling overhead
places.staff: fishmongers shouting in headbands, stall keepers pushing samples, a grandmother selling dried squid, shoppers with bulging bags

places.name: Yanaka
places.desc: old wooden streets behind a temple quarter, a little shopping street of croquettes and cat figures, a long stone stair at sunset, and cats on every wall
places.staff: an old woman sweeping her doorstep, a croquette seller, a photographer whispering, cats on walls and roofs

places.name: Ramen Kamejirō
places.desc: a twelve-seat counter under a red lantern in an Asakusa back street: a pot of pork-bone broth that's never gone cold in forty years, a ticket machine by the door
places.staff: the master works in silence; his daughter calls the orders and teases the regulars; old men at the counter, a line outside at lunch

places.name: Tsukimi Inari Shrine
places.desc: a small fox shrine up mossy steps in Yanaka: a short row of red gates, stone foxes in faded red bibs, a charm window, and a family home behind
places.staff: the priest and his wife, off at rituals; a neighbor sweeping the steps; a cat on the top step

places.name: Tokyo Station
places.desc: the red-brick station under its two domes: a river of suits at the ticket gates, bullet trains behind, underground streets of bento and sweets, and a glass-hall plaza a short walk away
places.staff: white-gloved attendants, bento sellers calling out, a hen party in matching sashes, solo travelers with suitcases, commuters walking fast

places.name: Asahina Trading
places.desc: a glass-and-steel trading company headquarters of forty floors: a marble lobby behind turnstile gates, a ground-floor coffee counter, a free sky lobby on top, and lit windows long after dark
places.staff: receptionists in matching scarves, guards bowing at the gates, employees on lunch runs, night cleaners, couriers

places.name: Tsubakiya Ginza
places.desc: a grand Ginza department store: handbags and perfume upstairs, and below ground the food hall of lit glass counters, sweets, sushi, pickles, bento and gift boxes, with clerks calling out samples
places.staff: clerks bowing at every counter, sample-holders, shoppers in good coats, a white-gloved lift attendant, an old woman choosing a melon

places.name: Ginza Chūō-dōri
places.desc: Ginza's grand avenue of flagship stores and old counters: doormen in white gloves, small galleries on upper floors, and on weekend afternoons the whole roadway closed to cars and given to walkers
places.staff: doormen in white gloves, staff bowing at the doors, window-gazing couples, solo travelers, a steward with a whistle

places.name: Izakaya Tetsuro
places.desc: a noisy izakaya in one brick arch under the Yūrakuchō railway tracks: a red lantern, a smoky yakitori grill by the door, plastic stools in the street and a train rumbling over every few minutes
places.staff: the master grills at the door; servers shout orders; office groups in loosened ties; a regular asleep in the corner

places.name: Imperial Palace East Gardens
places.desc: old Edo Castle's moat and stone walls, with the free East Gardens inside: broad lawns, a pond garden, the base of a vanished tower, and outside, the running loop around the whole palace
places.staff: runners in bright gear, guards handing out tokens, a cycling club resting by the moat, a gardener raking gravel

places.name: Ginza Kabuki Hall
places.desc: a kabuki theater of pale stone and dark wood built around one great hall: a plum-and-gold curtain, sweets counters in the lobby, and a gallery that climbs to the ceiling
places.staff: ushers in kimono, bento sellers, a circle of friends in matching scarves seated in a row, couples in good clothes, stagehands in black

places.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
places.desc: narrow lanes of seafood stalls, knife shops and rolled-omelet counters beside the old market site: foam crates on ice, hand-lettered signs, and a line at every sushi counter before the sun is high
places.staff: stall keepers calling prices, fishmongers with long knives, delivery carts, chefs buying, a company outing in matching caps

places.name: Seiwa General Hospital
places.desc: a big city hospital of white corridors and number-ticket machines: a packed morning waiting hall, wards of four beds, a quiet rooftop garden and an emergency entrance on the side street that never closes
places.staff: nurses in pastel scrubs moving fast, doctors with juniors trailing, patients with drip stands, old people holding numbered tickets

places.name: Odaiba Seaside Park
places.desc: a long man-made beach facing the bay, with Rainbow Bridge and the skyline across the water: a boardwalk, a small copy of a famous statue, windsurfers offshore, and signs that say no swimming
places.staff: joggers and dog walkers on the boardwalk, couples on the sand, windsurf instructors, a photographer with a tripod

places.name: Rainbow Bridge walkway
places.desc: a long fenced footpath on the lower deck of a white suspension bridge: wind, ships far below, Tokyo Tower orange to the north and the bay lights to the south
places.staff: walkers and photographers, a few solo travelers, friends stopping at the viewing points, a guard at the Shibaura gate

places.name: Odaiba Harbor Mall
places.desc: a harbor-front mall of terraced shops and food courts, with Kaien, a fifteen-meter white-and-teal robot, standing in the plaza beside a big screen for ball games and a roof terrace
places.staff: shop clerks in matching aprons, trade buyers with lanyards, a roving mascot, jerseys on game nights

places.name: Lumen Digital Art Museum
places.desc: a warehouse of dark rooms where light is the art: a hall of hanging paper lanterns that whisper, a long table that serves projected meals, a room of a hundred glowing clocks
places.staff: attendants in black with penlights, couples whispering, photographers hunting angles, a ticket desk with a timed-entry line

places.name: Tokyo Bay Exhibition Center
places.desc: an upside-down pyramid of glass and steel over a plaza of echoing concrete: a different fair every week, hall after hall of booths, and queues that begin before the first train
places.staff: event crews unrolling cable, buyers with lanyards on trade days, security with queue signs, vendors hauling boxes

places.name: Toyosu Market
places.desc: an enormous glass-and-steel wholesale market at dawn: turret trucks weaving between mountains of ice boxes, buyers in boots and caps, and a gallery above where visitors watch the tuna auction
places.staff: workers in white boots and aprons on turret trucks, auctioneers with bells, buyers with flashlights, visitors on the gallery

places.name: Wave TV Studios
places.desc: a glass-fronted television station on the waterfront: a lobby with a glowing wave sculpture, studios with red lights over the doors, a canteen, and a stage door where fans wait
places.staff: a guard at the gate, runners with headsets and clipboards, hair-and-makeup staff, guests in robes, a retirees' club in the lobby

places.name: Roppongi Crossing
places.desc: the junction under the expressway where two avenues cross: taxi queues, touts with flyers, a corner café everyone uses as a meeting spot, neon and a hum from the road overhead
places.staff: touts with flyers; taxi drivers in white gloves; police on patrol; clubbers meeting friends; a kebab-cart vendor

places.name: Club Undertow
places.desc: three floors of a former printing works: a basement main floor under a wall of speakers, a lounge bar on the ground floor, a roof terrace to cool off on
places.staff: door staff checking IDs; bartenders pouring fast; DJs in the booth; security in black tees; clubbers speaking five languages

places.name: Meridian Hills Sky Museum
places.desc: an art museum and sky deck at the top of a tower: long white galleries, a glass-walled deck over the whole city, and a night view that runs to the bay
places.staff: ticket staff in dark uniforms; gallery guards; a docent murmuring to a group of retirees; solo visitors and couples at the glass

places.name: Tokyo Tower
places.desc: the orange-and-white steel tower, 333 meters high: a main deck at 150 meters with a glass floor, a top deck at 250, and lights from sunset until midnight
places.staff: ticket staff; elevator attendants who bow at each floor; couples; exchange students and solo travelers; a photographer at the tower's foot

places.name: Azabu-Jūban
places.desc: an old shopping street below the towers: bakeries, a taiyaki stand, soba shops, a flower stall, shopkeepers who know every regular, and a temple's ancient ginkgo a short walk away
places.staff: shopkeepers sweeping their doorsteps; old residents with shopping carts; embassy staff buying bread; a taiyaki maker turning the irons

places.name: Lounge Ninth Floor
places.desc: a cocktail lounge on the ninth floor of a quiet tower: low sofas, a window wall facing Tokyo Tower, a long bar with one bartender, and prices nobody mentions
places.staff: a bartender in a white jacket; a host checking reservations at the door; regulars with bottles in a cabinet

places.name: The Crown & Anchor
places.desc: a British-style pub with dark wood, a dartboard, a long bar with hand pumps, football on a big screen and a crowd that sounds like four continents
places.staff: the landlord pulling pints; bar staff who switch languages mid-order; regulars on their stools; a cook in the back

places.name: Pole Star
places.desc: a basement stage with three chrome poles under blue light, a bar and low tables, and house rules posted by the door: watch, tip, don't touch; dancers here are athletes in sport costumes
places.staff: a bouncer at the door; a bartender; the house manager; dancers off stage with towels and water bottles; quiet regulars

places.name: Yokohama Chinatown
places.desc: Japan's biggest Chinatown: ten red-and-gold gates, lanterns over narrow streets, steam from bun stalls, a hundred restaurants, fortune tellers at folding tables and two temples among the shops
places.staff: bun vendors, cooks at open woks, fortune tellers at folding tables, a hen party in matching sashes, couples sharing a bun

places.name: Minato Mirai waterfront
places.desc: the glossy bay: a giant Ferris wheel with a clock face, tall towers, red-brick warehouses turned into shops and halls, and a wide promenade over the water where couples sit until the lights come on
places.staff: couples on benches, photographers with tripods, warehouse shop clerks, joggers, a busker with a keyboard, office workers on break

places.name: Yamashita Park
places.desc: a long seafront park along the bay: a promenade of benches, a rose garden, a fountain, and an old pre-war ocean liner moored at one end, white and quiet, with ship horns across the water
places.staff: couples walking, dog walkers, wedding photographers, a volunteer guide at the liner, joggers, a man selling roasted chestnuts

places.name: Isezaki Mall
places.desc: the long neon shopping arcade a few minutes from the station: pawn shops, pachinko roar, diners, secondhand bookstores, buskers on corners, hand-lettered sale signs, everybody's business everybody's
places.staff: shopkeepers sweeping doorsteps, buskers on corners, pawnbrokers behind glass, pachinko regulars, delivery bikes, old men on benches

places.name: Noge alleys
places.desc: a maze of cramped alleys by the river: standing bars, three-stool counters, hand-written menus, grilled-skewer smoke, red lanterns and the cheapest drinks in the city
places.staff: bar owners calling regulars by name, salarymen in loosened ties, old couples at counters, a street performer, cats in doorways

places.name: Club Hibiscus
places.desc: a hostess club on the second floor of an Isezaki building: eight velvet sofas, a faded hibiscus mural, a karaoke screen, and a mama who greets every guest by name
places.staff: a young bartender, four hostesses on a quiet night, a doorman in a vest, a regular nursing one bottle

places.name: Home Run Alley
places.desc: a batting center under a net-covered lot: twelve cages, ball machines of different speeds, a home-run board, a vending machine of canned coffee, and an owner who shouts advice from the bench
places.staff: a part-timer retrieving balls, regulars swinging after work, an old man heckling from the bench

places.name: Parlor Tenpai
places.desc: a smoky second-floor mahjong parlor off an Isezaki alley: six green-felt tables, the clatter of tiles, a hand-lettered "no betting" sign everyone reads with a straight face, and a master who never looks up
places.staff: the master behind a counter of tea, a part-timer carrying drinks, regulars at their usual tables, an old woman knitting

places.name: Ichō Park
places.desc: a small ginkgo park a few streets from the arcade: a bandstand, a few benches, a tap, a path under the trees, and a neighborhood of tents and blue tarps where people without homes keep each other company
places.staff: a man sweeping the path, a woman tending potted herbs, a few people playing shogi, neighbors dropping off bread

places.name: Hakone-Yumoto
places.desc: the hot-spring town at the station gate: a narrow street of souvenir shops and bun counters by the Hayakawa river, steam from the vents, a little red mountain train waiting
places.staff: shopkeepers offering samples, a bun-steamer in a white cap, travelers with wheeled bags, an old man hosing his doorstep

places.name: Ryokan Kasumi-sō
places.desc: a family ryokan up a steep lane: a lantern gate, a dark-wood lobby of slippers, a tatami corridor to eight rooms, a garden, an outdoor rock bath under the cedars
places.staff: the okami in kimono at the door; room attendants carrying trays; a cook behind a sliding door; guests in yukata

places.name: Lake Ashi
places.desc: an old volcanic crater filled with water: the red shrine gate standing in the lake at Moto-Hakone, cruise boats dressed as pirate galleons, cedars on the shore, Mt. Fuji beyond the hills on clear days
places.staff: a boat attendant at the pier, retirees on a club trip, a rowboat man in a straw hat by the dock, couples on benches

places.name: Ōwakudani
places.desc: a steaming valley of yellow rock and the smell of sulfur: the ropeway station above it, a shop selling black eggs by the bag, a trail through the steam, Fuji beyond on clear days
places.staff: egg-shop staff in aprons, a trail guard with a whistle, a university hiking club in matching caps, a ropeway attendant

places.name: Kirigaoka Sculpture Garden
places.desc: an open-air sculpture garden on a wooded hillside: steel, stone and bronze among cedars, a lawn of reeds that ring in the wind, a café terrace over the valley
places.staff: guides in gray aprons, a café barista, a guard on a stool, art students with sketchbooks, couples on benches

stories.setup: A woman with a tablet and a lanyard stops {{user}} on Center Gai with a bright smile: a two-minute lifestyle survey, and a free "skin analysis" voucher at the end. The tablet asks for name, email and mobile number before the first question. A man behind her has just walked away from the same stand, annoyed, tapping at his phone.

choices.label: Read the small print
choices.text: the "free" voucher is a ¥12,000 beauty-course sign-up; she shrugs and turns to the next person
choices.rumor: a survey stand on Center Gai signs people up for beauty courses

fail.text: you tap through and a ¥3,000 deposit is charged
fail.rumor: a survey stand on Center Gai signs people up for beauty courses

choices.label: Give a fake number
choices.text: she types it without checking and hands over the voucher; it only works with a real number
choices.fact: {u} gave a fake number to a survey stand

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: she follows three steps calling "just two minutes!" while the man behind laughs at you both
choices.rumor: the survey stand on Center Gai won't take no
choices.fact: {u} dodged a survey stand at {0}

stories.setup: Kaito sits at a machine with his tray empty and his phone buzzing face-down on the ledge, the same notification over and over. He sees {{user}} and grins too brightly: "One more and it hits, I swear." The machine's lights spin and the row's other players stare straight ahead, not one of them looking at him.

choices.label: Tell him to stop for today
choices.text: he pockets his last coins and walks out beside you

fail.text: "Next round," he says and sits

choices.label: Tell him to stop for today
choices.text: he pockets his last coins and walks out beside you

fail.text: "Next round," he says and sits

choices.fact: {u} learned Kaito borrowed from a loan app

choices.label: Play the machine next to his
choices.text: Kaito cheers either way

choices.label: Walk past
choices.text: he looks down at the machine instead of at you
choices.fact: {u} saw Kaito at the pachinko parlor and left him to it

stories.setup: A crêpe cook leans out of the stand and presses a paper cone into {{user}}'s hands: a birthday crêpe with a candle and a sparkler, not yet lit. "Hold this and look like it's yours!" Five women in cat-ear headbands crouch behind a costume rack, shushing each other; their friend, the birthday woman, is coming back from the restroom any second. The line behind {{user}} has started to mutter.

choices.label: Hold it and play along
choices.text: the birthday woman shrieks and laughs, her friends surge out singing, and a stranger's phone catches all of you; they insist you take the first bite

fail.text: the sparkler spits onto your sleeve; they laugh anyway, and so do you

choices.label: Light it and start the song
choices.text: the birthday woman arrives mid-verse, mortified, then delighted, and her friends take over the chorus
choices.fact: {u} helped surprise a stranger's birthday at {0}

choices.label: Hand it back to the cook
choices.text: he sighs and hides it under the counter; the surprise falls flat, the friends groan and the line shuffles on
choices.rumor: a birthday surprise fell flat on Takeshita

stories.when: weekend: yes; period: midmorning or afternoon
stories.setup: A Shinto wedding procession crosses the gravel courtyard: a priest, shrine maidens, the couple, the bride in white under a red paper umbrella, family in black behind. Two visitors with a long lens step onto the path ahead of them, aiming at the bride's face, and don't see the priest's raised hand. The nearest shrine staff member is far across the stones.

choices.label: Explain the custom quietly
choices.text: the visitors lower the camera and bow, the procession passes, and the priest gives you a nod

fail.text: they only half understand, and the whole procession has to stop and wait for them to move

choices.label: Wave over a staff member
choices.text: a white-robed man walks quickly across the gravel and guides the visitors aside, bowing his apologies to the family
choices.fact: {u} called a shrine attendant to steer visitors away from a wedding at {0}

choices.label: Bow and let them pass
choices.text: the procession steps around the visitors like water around stones; the nearest relative bows back, and you stand a long moment in the quiet
choices.rumor: a stranger bowed to a wedding at Meiji Jingū

stories.setup: Demo night starts in twenty minutes. Rina stands at the whiteboard in a blazer over a hoodie, rehearsing her pitch for the guest investor to an empty room, a phone on speaker timing her. She sees {{user}}, says "be the investor", and presses the timer: nine minutes. The last slide has numbers crossed out in two colors.

choices.label: Give honest feedback
choices.text: you spot the slide that will make an investor stop; Rina nods

fail.text: you nitpick the wrong slide and she thanks you flatly

choices.label: Ask about the runway
choices.text: she says "long enough" and starts the slide again
choices.fact: {u} asked Rina about money

choices.label: Ask about the runway
choices.text: she glances at the door and says it quietly: twelve weeks, if nobody tells payroll
choices.fact: {u} learned Hikari Labs has about twelve weeks of money

choices.label: Cheer her on from the back row
choices.text: she resets the timer and runs it again

choices.label: Call in the favor from Hakone
choices.text: she owes you one and knows it, so she drops the act: twelve weeks of money, maybe less
choices.fact: {u} called in a favor and learned how short Hikari Labs' money is

stories.setup: A brown leather wallet lies at the curb just before the lights change; the crowd steps over it. A man in a grey cap lingers three steps away, watching the wallet more than the lights. A woman beside {{user}} murmurs that it's been there a while. The police box on the square is a short walk away.

choices.label: Pick it up
choices.text: you spot the man's partner drifting behind you and hand the wallet to the police box; the pair slips away
choices.rumor: a bait wallet works the crossing

fail.text: your hands are full when someone bumps you and your own wallet is lighter by ¥3,000

choices.label: Tell the police box
choices.text: the officer checks the wallet; it holds nothing but a train ticket, and he thanks you
choices.fact: {u} reported a suspicious wallet at {0}

choices.label: Step over it
choices.text: a minute later a stranger picks it up and a woman's bag is lifted in the crush
choices.rumor: pickpockets work the crossing with a bait wallet
choices.fact: {u} saw a bait wallet at {0}

stories.setup: A young man in a stiff new suit stands frozen in the middle of the west concourse, staring at a map on his phone. People flow around him like water around a rock. It's his first morning at a new company, orientation starts at nine, and he has followed the signs for twenty minutes. He's close to tears. Nobody else has stopped.

choices.label: Walk him there
choices.text: Three corridors and a staircase later he reaches the door with a minute to spare. He pushes a thank-you note, scribbled on a page torn from his notebook, into your hand.
choices.rumor: a stranger walked a lost new hire to his first day
choices.fact: {u} got a lost new hire to his first day from {0}

fail.text: You both end up in the wrong tower's lobby. He sprints away apologizing.

choices.label: Flag down an attendant
choices.text: A gloved attendant takes him by the elbow and leads him off at a brisk pace. He looks back and bows from far away.

choices.label: Point at a sign
choices.text: He nods, thanks you and vanishes into the crowd. You never learn whether he made it.
choices.fact: {u} pointed a lost man at a sign in {0} and never learned if he made it

stories.setup: A young tout of twenty-one steps into {{user}}'s path with the practiced line: "Drinks, one hour, all you can drink, three thousand yen." His voice shakes on the third word. Behind him a senior tout watches from the corner with his arms folded. The young man has been on the job three weeks, is short of his quota tonight, and keeps glancing at the older man.

choices.label: Refuse with a smile
choices.text: He lets out a breath, whispers "thanks for not shouting" and tells you which stairwell on the next block is honest.
choices.rumor: a young tout in Kabukichō pointed someone to an honest bar
choices.fact: {u} was kind to a nervous tout at {0}

fail.text: The senior tout steps in and follows you half a block, pushing the price down and down.

choices.label: Follow him in
choices.text: The bar charges ¥6,000 in seat and drink fees for two weak drinks. At the door the young man bows low and won't meet your eyes.
choices.fact: {u} was overcharged at a bar in {0}

choices.label: Ask how his night is going
choices.text: He's three weeks in and sleeping at a friend's. You buy him a canned coffee, and he tells you which clubs treat their staff fairly.
choices.rumor: a tout says Lounge Velvet's mama is fair to her staff

stories.setup: On the curb outside a host club a woman in her twenties sits in last night's dress, her phone open to a bank app, and cries without making a sound. She owes ¥400,000 on a tab, and the host she's fond of has said he'll "sort something out". A passing host glances at her and keeps walking. A loan office's flyer is crumpled in her fist. She doesn't ask for help, and she doesn't wave anyone away.

examples.name: Mio
examples.description: {{char}} is Mio Hayasaka, 22, an art student at Hijiri University, from Sendai, who works night shifts at a Kōenji convenience store. Small, with an ash-pink bob and paint-stained overalls. Sunny, scattered and always broke; she talks fast, and Tōhoku words slip out when she's excited. She wants to finish her degree. Secretly she is failing two classes and hides it from her parents; the night shifts pay her tuition. She moved into the share house the same month as Chloe, and Friday karaoke has been their ritual ever since. Ren fixes her bike and she feeds him when he's broke. Linh buys breakfast after her night shifts and they talk while Mio restocks. She thinks Chloe is the one leaving drawings of her on the fridge.
examples.personality: sunny, scattered, generous, hides her worry behind jokes
examples.first_mes: *Mio sweeps the same square of floor for the third time, one earbud in, a sketchbook half-hidden under the register.* Welcome, welcome! It's dead tonight, but the rice-balls are fresh.
examples.look: Ash-pink bob, small, paint-stained overalls
examples.voice: Fast and bright; Tōhoku words slip out when excited

examples.name: Ren
examples.description: {{char}} is Ren Kujō, 26, bassist of Paper Lanterns, who books the bands and works the door at Basement Moon. Tall and lanky, shaggy shoulder-length black hair, stubble, a worn denim jacket over band tees. Slow, few words, dry jokes; he avoids arguments. He wants the band to matter. Secretly he keeps a notebook of songs about Nanami that he has never played. They dated three years and broke up last winter when he wouldn't move in with her; still in the band, still awkward. He started the band with Kaito years ago, playing for free in Saitama bars. Chloe is its loudest fan, Mio feeds him when he's broke, and Seo-yeon, who serves at Kissa Shirakaba where he reads, has noticed his notebook.
examples.personality: easygoing, dry, conflict-avoidant, quietly romantic
examples.first_mes: *Ren crouches by a speaker stack at Basement Moon, coiling a cable round his elbow, a bass case propped against the wall.* Doors are at seven; don't touch the amp, it's older than both of us.

examples.name: Chloe
examples.description: {{char}} is Chloe Bennett, 28, an English teacher from Manchester, three years in Tokyo. Tall, freckled, curly auburn hair in a claw clip, cardigans and sneakers. Outgoing and homesick underneath; blunt Manchester English with Japanese phrases mixed in, cheerful swearing, "mate" and "love" for everyone. She wants to stay in Tokyo for good. Secretly her school stops sponsoring visas next spring, and unless she finds another sponsor she has to leave. She sings every Friday with Mio, drags Haru out of their room for sentō nights, and is the loudest fan of Ren's band. She met Lisa at The Crown & Anchor; Lisa takes her clubbing and she teaches Lisa English swearing. At the pub Lucas pours her pints and they swear at football; Jake is her pub-quiz rival.
examples.personality: outgoing, blunt, warm, loud, homesick
examples.first_mes: *Chloe blows a curl out of her face and wipes the whiteboard with her cardigan sleeve.* Hiya, love, you the new student? Sit anywhere, the whiteboard's the only thing in here that bites.

examples.description: {{char}} is Haru Aoki, 24, a key animator at Studio Tsubame; they use they/them. Slim, with a bleached buzz cut, silver ear cuffs, a black hoodie and ink always on their fingers. Introverted and observant; they speak quietly and precisely, deadpan, and cut deep when it counts. Loyal to the few they let in. They want to make something that is their own. Secretly they leave anonymous drawings of Mio on the fridge, and they have a crush on her; Mio thinks Chloe does it. Chloe drags them out for sentō nights. Natsuki was a classmate at art school; she went into games, Haru into anime, and they still trade sketches. examples.name: Genzō
examples.description: {{char}} is Genzō Kamei, 55, master of Ramen Kamejirō for forty years. Short, broad-shouldered, a white towel tied around his shaved head, forearms marked by old burns, eyes that miss nothing. A widower who says ten words a day and means all of them; gruff with strangers, gentle with his daughter Ayaka, though he'd never say so. Secretly, the shop's lease ends this year and he hasn't told her. He speaks in short, blunt Tokyo-downtown sentences, calls everyone by their family name, and drops honorifics only for people he trusts. Thirty years ago he was engaged to Kyōko Shirai; they still meet at Sensō-ji every New Year for the midnight bell.

Crisp, formal and commanding at work, using surnames with "-san" and "-kun"; after a drink she softens. Brilliant, a perfectionist, lonely. She wants a quiet life she can't admit to. Secretly she is close to burning out and tells no one. She found Bar Kotori by accident two years ago and often comes on Fridays to sing; that is no secret. Rina is her younger sister; Reiko took the safe career their parents wanted, Rina quit it, and each thinks the other is wrong. She trained Daisuke three years ago. Mei translates for her team and is the only one she lets see her tired.

examples.name: Kanon
examples.description: {{char}} is Kanon Shiraishi, 22, a grown woman from Chiba who draws adult doujinshi and lives alone in a wooden apartment. Curvy, mint-dyed hair grown out to black roots, big round glasses, track pants, chipped black nail polish. Anxious, sharp-witted and starved for closeness; she talks in rapid, mumbled otaku references, then overshares. She wants to be touched and to be seen as an artist. Secretly she hasn't left the apartment for more than a convenience-store run in months, except for the summer fan convention, where she sells her book. She has an adult's worries (rent, loneliness, deadlines) and nothing childlike in her look or manner. Natsuki bought her book there.

examples.name: Airi
examples.description: {{char}} is Airi Mizusawa (a stage name), 26, a veteran AV actress from Osaka: a grown woman with a career, fans and TV spots. Glossy chestnut waves, a designer coat, sunglasses even at night, a laugh you hear across the bar. Frank, funny and unashamed, in Osaka dialect; confident, warm and tired of being a symbol. She wants a good exit and a life afterward. Secretly she has a retirement date her agency doesn't know about yet. Her work is off-screen and never shown; she knows her contract and her rights under the 2022 law. She drinks at Bar Kotori because Kyōko never asks about her work, and she took Momo, the rookie, under her wing.

examples.name: Momo
examples.description: {{char}} is Momo Sakuraba (a stage name), 21, a rookie AV actress from Fukuoka: a grown woman, with no childlike role in her work or manner. Tall and athletic from years of volleyball, short brown hair, sporty clothes, a nervous smile. Bubbly, in Fukuoka dialect, and apologizing when nervous; eager, anxious and braver than she looks. She wants a steady income and an ordinary life later. Secretly her family thinks she works at a gym in Tokyo. Her work is off-screen; she read her contract three times and knows the 2022 law lets her cancel it. Airi took her under her wing, and she takes Lisa's pole-fitness class.
